elements.evidence: "Customer ... may terminate this Agreement or any Statement of Work for convenience"
"Contractor shall refund, on a pro-rata basis, any prepaid fees for Services not performed as of the effective date of termination"

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term
elements.evidence: Term is evergreen — "shall continue until terminated by either party" — so no committed term exists and the condition is demonstrably absent; Contractor's convenience right in (a) applies only "At any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding".
"upon 30 days' written notice" (30 days, outside the 60–90 day fallback band)

elements.element: Early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee is imposed; refund runs to Customer's benefit.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at end of a term on 90 days' notice
elements.evidence: "either party may terminate this Agreement for any or no reason upon fifteen (15) days advance notice" remains untouched

offending_extra_words: Customer may terminate under this Paragraph 6(c) at its convenience.
(which for purposes of this Paragraph 6 means Company)
reasons: The preferred level is complete: a Customer convenience right on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and no committed term during which Contractor could exercise convenience termination.
Minimality fails: the trailing sentence "Customer may terminate under this Paragraph 6(c) at its convenience." duplicates the convenience right already granted in the first sentence and adds nothing.

Minimality also fails on the alias gloss "(which for purposes of this Paragraph 6 means Company)" — the Agreement already defines "Company", so the insertion should simply say "Company" rather than introduce a new defined party label.

Note (not a deviation): the inserted text is numbered (c) within the displayed Paragraph 2 block but self-references "this Paragraph 6"; the cross-reference should be conformed to the paragraph in which it actually sits to avoid a dangling reference.

Fallback is not satisfied as its own bargain (30 days is outside the 60–90 day band and Contractor retains a 15-day convenience right), but this is immaterial because the locked preferred level is met.
